story.title: Inside Muscat International Airport's New Hangar, Oman Launches Its First Dedicated Aircraft Maintenance Company
story.seo_title: Oman Air & GMF AeroAsia Launch Oman GMF Technic MRO Hub
story.meta_description: Oman Air and Indonesia's GMF AeroAsia launch Oman GMF Technic at Muscat International Airport, establishing Oman's first aircraft MRO company.

detail.extracted_title: Inside Muscat International Airport's New Hangar, Oman Launches Its First Dedicated Aircraft Maintenance Company
detail.excerpt: Oman Air and Indonesia's GMF AeroAsia have formed Oman GMF Technic, bringing heavy aircraft overhaul and specialized aviation engineering careers home to Muscat.
detail.article_html:
Walk onto the floor of the newly inaugurated aircraft maintenance hangar at Muscat International Airport, and the scale of the steel roof trusses overhead tells you what the building was made for. Widebody airliners that once had to fly thousands of kilometers abroad for major structural inspections and heavy overhauls can now roll directly off the Muscat runway and into a climate-controlled bay staffed by Omani and international aviation engineers.

Inside that hangar on Wednesday, national carrier Oman Air and GMF AeroAsia—Indonesia's leading aircraft maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) specialist—officially launched Oman GMF Technic. Unveiled under the patronage of H.E. Eng. Said bin Hamood Al Maawali, Minister of Transport, Communications and Information Technology and Chairman of Oman Air, alongside H.E. Sultan bin Salim Al Habsi, Minister of Finance, the joint venture establishes the first specialized aircraft MRO company in the Sultanate of Oman.

Keeping Heavy Maintenance and Engineering Value in Oman

In commercial aviation, keeping a fleet safe and airworthy requires two distinct tiers of engineering work: day-to-day Line Maintenance between flights, and intensive Base Maintenance, where an aircraft is taken out of service for weeks so technicians can inspect its airframe, engines, avionics, and landing gear down to the bare metal.

Until now, airlines operating in the Sultanate had to send much of their heavy maintenance work to external MRO facilities outside the country. Built inside the new maintenance complex opened by the Civil Aviation Authority at Muscat International Airport, Oman GMF Technic will deliver both heavy Base Maintenance and Line Maintenance locally—serving Oman's domestic carriers while competing for maintenance contracts from regional and international airlines flying between Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe.

Training a New Generation of Omani Aviation Engineers

For Nasser bin Ahmed Al Sharji, Chief Executive Officer of Oman Air, the joint venture is as much about the people working on the hangar floor as the aircraft parked inside it. By pairing Muscat's modern hangar infrastructure with GMF AeroAsia's decades of international certification and technical systems, the company creates a long-term training ground for Omani aviation engineers and licensed aircraft technicians.

Andi Fahrurrozi, Chief Executive Officer of GMF AeroAsia, noted that the partnership is structured around direct knowledge transfer and hands-on technical instruction. As Omani engineers work side by side with senior MRO specialists on complex airframe overhauls, Oman builds sovereign engineering capability at home while exporting high-value technical services across the wider aviation corridor linking the Indian Ocean, the Gulf, and Europe.

  • Oman Daily
detail.instagram_caption:
National carrier Oman Air and Indonesian aviation engineering specialist GMF AeroAsia have officially launched Oman GMF Technic, establishing the first dedicated aircraft maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) company in the Sultanate of Oman. Announced inside the newly inaugurated aircraft maintenance hangar opened by the Civil Aviation Authority at Muscat International Airport, the joint venture marks a structural leap for Oman's aviation and logistics sector.

Oman GMF Technic will provide both heavy Base Maintenance and day-to-day Line Maintenance for domestic carriers as well as regional and international airlines. By performing complex airframe inspections and overhauls inside Muscat International Airport, the facility reduces reliance on overseas maintenance providers while attracting foreign airline fleets operating across the crossroads of the Middle East, Asia, Africa, and Europe.

Alongside its commercial operations, the joint venture establishes a specialized technical training and knowledge-transfer pipeline with GMF AeroAsia, equipping Omani aviation engineers and technicians with international MRO certifications and long-term career pathways.

Read the full analysis at omanspire.om (link in bio).
